newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise Oil up after top-end profits.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise Oil up after top-end profits.

text.p: Shares in Enterprise Oil Plc rose in early trading on Thursday, after the company posted results at the top end of analyst expectations.
Net income rose to 73.8 million stg from 46.5 million a year before, compared with forecasts in a range between 65.1 million stg and 80.0 million, and the stock was up 5-1/2p at 530 by 0718 GMT.
"It was an excellent set of figures, the results are at the top end and we have got the follow-through from higher oil prices," said Jurjen Lunshof, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
"The company has surplus cash flow, debts are very low, it all looks very good on paper," Lunshof said. "The company's rehabilitation continues and we continue to be strong buyers of the stock."
Elizabeth Butler, analyst at Panmure Gordon, said the figures were good but the outlook for the stock was more dependent on expectations for the price of oil.

As an exploration and production company Enterprise is more directly sensitive to swings in the price of oil than groups such as British Petroleum and Shell, which also have large downstream operations.
But Butler said some investors may be shying away from a stock which has risen sharply in recent months, concerned that higher oil prices may not last.

"My feeling is that a lot of people are not buying into the sector because the price has just run up," she said. "But even with Iraqi oil in the system I don't see a surplus in crude and there could even be a deficit next year."
Analysts also welcomed Enterprise's entry into two new oil-producing areas, the Gulf of Mexico and the Middle East.
"They are getting into two quite interesting areas at a quite advantageous price," Lunshof said.
After touching a five-year high of 533p in early trade, by 0831 GMT, the initial spurt had fizzled to leave the stock down 1p at 523-1/2.
